I farm 20 mu here in Quzhou, wheat in winter and maize after. I have been doing this since I was young, same as my father. With 6 mouths to feed and some of us working outside, I cannot take chances with the harvest.

For the wheat this autumn, I will plant the same Jimai variety the seed shop sells — most neighbors use it and it does well on our land. I plough before sowing because the maize stubble needs to go in. At sowing I put about 2 bags of compound fertilizer per mu as base — that is roughly 50 kg of the 18-18-18 type. Then at green-up in spring I top-dress with urea, about 20 kg per mu. That gives me enough nitrogen. I do not want yellow wheat in March — my neighbor Old Wang had that two years ago and he lost a lot.

Irrigation on wheat: I water before winter to protect the roots, then at jointing in March, and again at heading if the spring is dry. Usually 3 times from the well. Pesticide I spray twice — once for aphids and once mixed with the herbicide.

For the summer maize, I do not plough — just straight seed into the wheat stubble, no-tillage with the seeder. Saves time and diesel. I use Zhengdan or whatever hybrid the dealer recommends that year. At sowing I put compound fertilizer, 40 kg per mu, then top-dress urea 25 kg per mu when the maize is knee-high. Maize eats a lot of nitrogen, I have seen that myself.

Maize I usually only irrigate once, at tasseling if July rain is short. Pesticide twice — for armyworm and borer. Last year my yield was about 550 kg maize and 470 kg wheat per mu, I expect about the same.
